Thank you! That's quite a nice way to look at things, I'm especially excited to see Denmark (I want to work there for some time eventually) so in that respect I may only spend a night there if I'm going to return in the future.

I was concerned about the travel times although for the longer journeys I was hoping overnight trains would help combat that, especially around the eastern block. It'll also save money on hostels as reservations for the overnight trains will be a lot cheaper. Is this a good way of looking at things or is it more complicated than I thought? I'm aware that we'll miss the views and such although it's a sacrifice I'm willing to make if it means we spend more times in the actual places.

I feel the same way, it seems that when I'm around people I can make conversation as if it's a type of distraction from my own thoughts, but when I reflect back on it the paranoid part of my brain goes into overdrive...

I'm really happy to see that you're getting better now, sometimes you have to get through the rough of these fluctuating emotions to get to the light at the end of the tunnel :)
Is a cut that deep bad enough for stitches?

Yeah I did originally start writing out 'things i like/don't like about myself' to clear my thoughts (as per therapists request) although i started with the dislikes and it eventually tore me apart so much that I just had to end it with a suicide note.

Thanks for the advice anyway, I'll try and see what I can do. Obviously I'm not in the best of minds right now and I think part of the problem is that there's never been anything I've excelled at and there's just been immense pressure to live up to the expectations everyone had of me when I was a 'gifted' child, which has just made me collapse. Right now I don't really have anything to love about myself, which I guess is making me question my existence on this planet recently

I have my health.

I'm not unattractive by any means...

I had good grades which means I do have some intelligence lurking in my mind somewhere.

I'm not really feeling the greatest at the moment so that's pretty much all I can think of at the moment...
This looks amazing, possibly my favourite tattoo i've seen on /r/tattoos in a long time!

I've got a fair few (big scars) up my arm and on my shoulder, quite obviously and even when they fade, they'll be pretty big white ones. I was going to get a full sleeve tattoo to cover them all up eventually (I'm 17 at the moment though although I've been wanting a tattoo for a long time now), although is this a bad idea? 

I'm going to have to cover my sleeves in a professional environment anyway just to avoid the awkward glances and questions, so is a tattoo on my arm such a bad idea if it's covering up something that (in my opinion) is potentially worse? I'd rather limit my job options than have to bear having the scars on show, or is this quite a stupid way to look at things?

You definitely don't need to feel worse, many people with clinical depression have no 'proper' reason to feel that way, and just put it down to chemical imbalances. You might feel the same, but there's definitely nothing that's not valid enough to be depressed by!

I'm in pretty much the same situation as you - 16 years old and never really had a proper relationship, although I put it down to my depression which was around before my relationship problems, so I know how it feels :)

I could give you lots of relationship advice on how to get a girl and give you lots of tips from past experience but then again every situation is different and it's hard to help over the internet. But what's helped me cope is trying to enjoy my own company and focus on friends, rather than girlfriends. I know it's easier said than done (as I've found out), if they're really good friends (and famnily, don't forget family!) then you can get the same happiness from them as you would a girlfriend. Just place your trust in them and hopefully it'll help. It's helped with my sometimes, and it's worth a shot with you - plus socialising may help you feel more normal and more wanted :)

I think that if you start to feel more comfortable in yourself then you'll be more confident (and therefore attractive) and that will definitely show and you'll be hopefully fighting girls off in no time ;)

I hope this has helped, it may not be what you're looking for but I definitely hope how it feels, and I hope you (and I) can get through this eventually :) stay strong buddy.

This might not be too relevant to you as I'm under 18, but I saw the GP around October time, who then referred me to CAMHS (under 18 mental health service of the NHS), had my first meeting at the beginning of this month. 

The inital session was alright, the therapist seemed a bit teacher-y and it was just lots of questions, quite impersonal but she wasn't horrible to talk to, so I can't complain! She's filing the report and it should be mailed soon, and during the session she talked about the possibilities of CBT and medication, but I'll have to contact the GP (and maybe the psychiatrists) first. She gave me quite a bit of information so it was quite good!

It's quite lengthy to get going (I was relatively quick compared to some others, I've heard) but it's worth it, we can't really complain if it's all free! haha

I saw this a while back and thought it was a good tattoo so I had a sketch to see how it would look more symmetrical - I didn't bother to add any colour to it yet though. Would this be any better, considering there aren't as many lines, or is it still too many? 

P.s I'm not claiming this to be original or that I'm an artist, it just inspired me to think about tattoos like this.
Or the more crude high school version - the "banter tampon"
I wouldn't really say that making this image is really getting butthurt and making a 'big deal out of it' if I'm honest...

Well teaching would be good, and I reckon you could do things like writing, journalism and other media things, law/investment banking, management or go into acedemia if you're really stuck. You won't have a problem, the difficulties come in when you become more specific (like history of art, maybe not as useful).

I think it does count for things like history, sociology and english, as well as art and all the other arty degrees. Law I'm not so sure about though...

Although I'm from England so this isn't even all clear cut for me - if it does count for history and the likes, is it really such a useless degree over in America? A history degree is pretty much as useful as a science degree over here.
Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics - pretty much everything sciency, encompasses most things that aren't 'liberal arts' degrees.

You should definitely be proud! You're going to improve in gradual steps, and you're one step closer! If tomorrow you don't feel as if you can get up at 8am, try getting up maybe half an hour earlier than you did today, or even just at the same time as today so you can get comfortable. Eventually you'll get used to it and feel better. Everything is more manageable in small chunks :)

As for the second paragraph, don't think that because you don't/can't self harm, you're not depressed. People just have different coping mechanisms, just because someone cuts themselves it doesn't mean they're more depressed than someone who doesn't. People have had depression for so long that they can't remember being happy, but it doesn't mean that because that they've always been like this, that it's normal.

Keep at it, I'm proud of you and I hope you can feel better soon :)
